The Delhi government has constituted three special committees to oversee the organisation of the upcoming Ramlila, Durga Puja and Chhath Puja festivals, it stated in a release on Saturday. Culture Minister Kapil Mishra will head the committees for Chhath Puja and Durga Puja celebrations while Social Welfare Minister Ravinder Indraj Singh will head the committee for Ramlila arrangements. The committees will review and ﬁnalise venues for the respective festivals and coordinate essential arrangements at the venues, the government said.

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) will provide new auto-tippers in all wards in east and north-east Delhi by October 15 to strengthen sanitation arrangements ahead of the festive season. The directions were issued by MCD Standing Committee chairperson Satya Sharma at a meeting with the MCD Commissioner to review sanitation arrangements in the Shahdara south and north zones. Ms. Sharma directed oﬃcials to increase auto-tippers where required to ensure uninterrupted door-to-door waste collection. She directed oﬃcials to install compactors, ensure cleaning of  dhalao ghars  and monitor private concessionaires.  PTI

More than 350 electors in Delhi’s draft electoral roll, who were ﬂagged for notic- es during the ongoing spe- cial  intensive  revision (SIR), have been marked “ineligible” for the ﬁnal electoral roll less than a month into the hearings process,  The Hindu  has learnt. About 200 of these are  in  the  Vikaspuri constituency. Delhi Chief Electoral Of- ﬁcer (CEO) Ashok Kumar has, meanwhile, warned Electoral Registration Of- ﬁcers (EROs), who alone hold the statutory power to mark an elector “ineligi- ble”, against taking such decisions without complet- ing the required veriﬁca- tions. The letter speciﬁcal- ly  instructed  that  no deletion should be made on “ﬂimsy or frivolous grounds”. Once a voter is marked ineligible, this can- not be rolled back at the le- vel of the ERO or even the State CEO, oﬃcials said. Apart from Vikaspuri, other  constituencies where voters have been marked ineligible so far in- clude Madipur, Malviya Na- gar, Sangam Vihar and

Tughlakabad. The 350- plus voters marked ineligi- ble were among 33.1 lakh names ﬂagged by the Elec- tion Commission (EC) of India for notices in the “unmapped” or “logical discrepancies” categories. These are voters who sub- mitted their enumeration forms during the enumera- tion phase of the SIR and appeared on the draft elec- toral roll published on Au- gust 31.

The process EROs told  The Hindu  that they can mark an elector ineligible on the EC’s soft- ware either by specifying that the elector did not ap- pear for their hearing after rescheduling attempts or in cases where documents produced by the elector

are found unsatisfactory. Merely not appearing for a hearing does not establish that an elector is ineligible to vote. The Vikaspuri ERO was not available for comment on  the  cases  or  the grounds on which the elec- tors were declared ineligi- ble. West District Election Oﬃcer (DEO) Hari Kallikat said the DEO had no auth- ority over the process. “It is under the statutory pow- ers of the ERO. They are supposed to pass a speak- ing order with the reason mentioned and upload it,” he said. An oﬃcial familiar with the Vikaspuri cases said some electors marked ineligible included those whose hearings had not been rescheduled despite the option being available.

A 45-year-old autorickshaw driver was killed and another man injured after an allegedly speeding car rammed into two vehicles in south-east Delhi’s Sukhdev Vi- har on Saturday morning, the police said, adding that the 21-year-old car driv- er has been arrested. The police identiﬁed the deceased as Mohd. Kalam, a resident of New Friends Colony, and the injured man as Md. Ba- blu, who lived under the Sukhdev Vihar metro station.  A case has been registered against the accused, Mohd. Talib, under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at the New Friends Colony police station. The car and the autorickshaw were found at the spot, and a crime team inspected the scene. Further investiga- tion is under way, the police added. According to the police, the accident occurred around 7 a.m. when the car rammed into Kalam’s autorickshaw be- fore hitting a cycle rickshaw. Kalam was taken to Escorts Hospital, where he was declared dead, while Mr. Bablu was treated for his injuries.

‘Cars had been racing’ An eyewitness, Jeet, claimed that two cars had been racing moments before the crash. “I heard a loud noise and turned to see that an accident had happened. Two cars were racing each other and one car rammed into the auto. By that time, the other car had ﬂed at high speed,” he said. He claimed that the car was travelling from the ﬂyover towards Shaheen Bagh and had three to four occupants who ﬂed after the crash. A video recorded by a passer-by showed the car extensively damaged, with its airbag deployed, and the autorickshaw badly crushed. (With inputs from PTI)

he Election Com- mission (EC) of In- dia on Saturday ex- tended the deadlines for ﬁling claims and objections and for the notice and dis- posal phase under Delhi’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with 93% of hearings pending and only 1.2 lakh applica- tions received for inclusion against 47.56 lakh electors left out of the draft roll. According to a press re- lease issued by the Delhi Chief Electoral Oﬃcer’s of- ﬁce, the deadline for ﬁling claims and objections has been extended from Sep- tember 30 to October 30, while the notice and dispo- sal phase has been extend- ed from October 29 to No- vember 30. Both phases began on August 31. The ﬁ- nal electoral roll will be pu- blished on December 4.
Slow progress According to data seen by The Hindu , only around 2 lakh hearings have been

completed so far, with 93% still pending three weeks into the phase. A total of 33.1 lakh electors were ﬂagged for notices over “no mapping” and “logical discrepancies”.  Progress has been slow amid a lack of clarity over the docu- ments required and re- quests for rescheduling, an oﬃcial said. Meanwhile, only 1.2 lakh applications for inclusion in the electo- ral roll have been received since the publication of the draft roll on August 31.
Lack of clarity Delhi Deputy Chief Electo- ral Oﬃcer Prashant Kumar

on Saturday said detailed directions on compliance with the EC directions, in- cluded BLOs being now re- quired to collect docu- ments and complete the process at the homes of noticees, would be issued in the coming week. “There are hearings al- ready scheduled for Sun- day, which will carry on as is. BLOs were already in- structed to collect docu- ments in case of logical dis- crepancies and complete the process at the elector’s home,” he said. While over 16 lakh notices have been delivered, an equal num- ber remain pending.

A Delhi court on Saturday deferred the hearing on an appeal ﬁled by four women wrestlers challenging the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in a sexual harassment case. The appeal, ﬁled on Friday, also challenged the acquittal of former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar on a criminal intimidation charge. Court staﬀ said Judge Dig Vinay Singh was on leave for training and the matter would be heard on Monday. On August 3, a magisterial court acquitted Brij Bhushan Singh, a BJP MP, in the sexual harassment case involving six women wrestlers, citing lack of evidence.  PTI
Court defers women wrestlers’ plea over Brij Bhushan acquittal

Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, Joint Com- missioner Nupur Prasad and senior oﬃcers inspect- ed Jahanpanah Forest and Deer Park in south Delhi late on Friday, reviewing lighting, CCTV coverage, boundary  walls,  gates, guards and access control following the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Astha Kunj Park on September

21. Similar assessments are under way across the city in coordination with civic agencies. More than 170 parks have been audited in south Delhi and 150 in south-east Delhi, oﬃcials told T he Hindu. South  Delhi  Deputy Commissioner of Police Anant Mittal said oﬃcers are assessing physical se- curity, speaking to park us- ers and residents and ﬂag- ging gaps to the agencies concerned.
Following the incident, police have increased pa- trolling around education-
al institutions and parks, all-woman PCR vans have been increased from 15 to
35, and women-centric ‘Pink Force’ and a ‘Pink Scooty’ squad have been formed.

‘Not the answer’ Meanwhile, the Delhi De- velopment Authority’s de- cision to restrict entry into its parks after sunset has drawn opposition from women students who said restricting access to public spaces was “not the answ- er to sexual violence”. On Friday, hundreds of

students from Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Gargi College and Kamala Nehru College marched on Siri Fort Road demanding better street lighting, more DTC buses, aﬀordable me- tro passes, shuttle services to metro stations, usable public toilets and stronger complaint  redressal mechanisms. The  students  also sought police sensitisation and fast-track courts for crimes against women.
